Already addressed in metadata.rs. The literal-string copy-paste the bead describes is gone: the three /set loop catch-all arms now route through a shared helper at metadata.rs:484 (create), 535 (update), 597 (destroy):

    Err(other) => { not_*.insert(id, unhandled_backend_set_error(&other)); }

The helper at helpers.rs:156-162 emits 'unhandled backend error variant: {e:?}' — the bead's second concern (literal-string telling the operator nothing about which variant fired) was resolved by bd:JMAP-826m.36 routing through the helper's {e:?} interpolation.

The bead's deeper refactor (fold all three Err arms into one backend_set_error_to_value helper) is more invasive and would diverge further from canonical mail-server (which still uses three-arm shape with literal strings at 32 sites across email/identity/mailbox/mdn/sieve/submission/vacation). Per the canonical-template propagation rule, that's a workspace-wide sweep, not a metadata-server-local change.

If the deeper refactor is desired, it should be filed as a workspace-wide canonical-template sync bead with mail-server as the first sibling to touch — metadata-server is the polished evolution that mail-server can be brought up to, not the other way around. Not filing that sweep bead myself: same opinion P3 cost-benefit as JMAP-ayoz.14's workspace sweep question, and the bead's metadata-server-local concern is already addressed.
